title: Check that edits to zedu.chat pages reach visitors and Google quickly, by Fri 4 Dec
description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026: the home page is sent with cache-control: s-maxage=31536000, which allows a shared cache such as Cloudflare to keep it for a year. We did not test how long an edit takes to appear, so this goal is to find out and fix it if needed.

Success looks like: change a harmless line on a test page, record how long until the live page shows it (fetch it with curl every few minutes), and report the result. If it takes more than a day, set a cache rule or revalidation so edits show within a day without hurting speed, and say which file or Cloudflare rule changed.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Check merged-vs-live first: two fixes on cybertron-integration still aren't on zedu.chat
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before measuring cache delay, check whether edits are deployed at all. On 22 Oct 2026, Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe cybertron-integration (214cb29) already has src/app/(homepage)/policy/layout.ts and terms-of-service/layout.ts, which set each page's own title and canonical. But live https://zedu.chat/policy and /terms-of-service still serve the home page title and canonical https://zedu.chat. Plan: a small script that, after each merge, curls a handful of pages and compares title, canonical and one changed string against the branch, reporting 'merged but not live'. That separates deploy lag (which branch production builds from) from cache lag (s-maxage).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Confirm whether pages update on deploy or on revalidation, then set revalidate only where needed
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Checked 22 Oct 2026: the home page sends Cache-Control: s-maxage=31536000 together with x-nextjs-prerender: 1, x-nextjs-cache: HIT and x-nextjs-stale-time: 300, while Cloudflare reports cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC. That points to Next.js static prerendering (its default year-long s-maxage) rather than Cloudflare holding the page, so an edit likely appears on the next deploy, not after a year. Plan: 1) deploy a harmless text change and poll with curl every 5 minutes, recording when it appears and the cache headers; 2) if content comes from a CMS or API rather than code, add a revalidate value per page so edits show within a day; 3) list the exact file or Cloudflare rule changed. Tasks: timing test (research), fix spec if needed (SEO).

acceptedWorkstreams.description: The home page is sent with s-maxage=31536000 plus x-nextjs-cache: HIT and x-nextjs-prerender: 1 (curl -I, 22 Oct 2026), so a prerendered page may be kept by shared caches until something purges it. Tasks: (1) make one harmless text change on a low-traffic page, then curl it every 5 minutes and log when the change appears, with response headers each time; (2) if it takes over a day, set an explicit revalidate on the (homepage) routes or add a Cloudflare purge step to the deploy, and say which in a short note; (3) repeat the test to confirm, and request reindexing for changed pages in Search Console.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Post-deploy propagation canary: after every deploy, prove one known rendered value went live within 2 minutes
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The one-off measurements and merged-vs-live check are covered; this makes the guarantee permanent. Plan: a tiny check that runs after each deploy, reads one known rendered value from a live page (an edited title or date), and fails loudly when it does not match what shipped - turning 'merged but not live' from something someone notices weeks later into a build-time alarm. Deliver the check plus the first week of results.

downvotes.reason: This duplicates accepted approach cmvjiirqb071w122mtq52vr0q, which already specifies a script after each merge comparing a handful of live titles, canonicals and one changed string against the branch and reporting merged-but-not-live. Reading one rendered value after deploy is the same check moved to a pipeline trigger; that trigger belongs in the existing implementation. The new two-minute guarantee and first week of results also need a real deployment cadence and owner approval, neither established here. Add the hook and agreed timing to the existing work rather than commission another overlapping monitor.
